scope: The pinned GR00T inference and training paths used by this reference. This assessment does not apply to arbitrary applications using the same Torch installation.

decision.selection: Retain the current Torch runtimes and document application applicability.
decision.reason: Preserve the qualified GR00T, CUDA and native-extension compatibility.
decision.scanner_disposition: These findings remain library findings; applicability evidence requires release/security review and is not scanner clearance.

validation_scope.method: Isolated CPU reproductions with Torch 2.10.0+cpu and Torch 2.7.1+cpu, plus exact-version upstream source review.
validation_scope.limitation: The invalid-input reproducers were not executed against the live GPU services. CPU behavior and common source establish affected code; they do not substitute for GPU compatibility testing.

policy_loading.symbol: Gr00tPolicy.__init__: AutoModel.from_pretrained, then model.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16) at line 102

backbone_loading.symbol: Qwen3 backbone: torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16 when loading BF16

optional_profiling.symbol: Conditional torch.profiler.profile around Trainer.train; no user-provided future or record handle

advisories.status: library remains affected, application exposure assessed
advisories.trigger: Save state_dict() from torch.ao.nn.quantized.Sigmoid(0.1, 5), then load it into Sigmoid(0.5, 10). The empty state dict omits output_scale and output_zero_point, so the new module retains 0.5 and 10.
advisories.observed_result: Both reviewed CPU versions retain the incorrect destination quantization parameters after load_state_dict.
advisories.application_assessment: The GR00T policy uses BF16 inference and the reviewed GR00T model/training sources contain no quantized Sigmoid usage. Its checkpoint path does not instantiate the affected module.
advisories.upstream_status: Issue 147818 remains open; no upstream fix was established during this review.
advisories.remaining_fix_scope: A versioned quantized-Sigmoid state serialization fix is needed in Torch. Legacy empty state dictionaries lack the original parameters and cannot be repaired automatically.

advisories.status: library remains affected, application exposure assessed
advisories.trigger: Directly call torch.ops.profiler._call_end_callbacks_on_jit_fut(torch.tensor(0), None). The native callback helper dereferences the null Future at fut->then.
advisories.observed_result: Both reviewed CPU versions exited with SIGSEGV in disposable subprocesses with core dumps disabled.
advisories.application_assessment: No direct call to the affected private operator or request mapping that supplies external future/record-handle inputs was identified in PGFR or pinned GR00T inference/training code. Optional GR00T training profiling is disabled by default; when enabled, it uses torch.profiler.profile around Trainer.train.
advisories.upstream_status: Issue 147722 remains open; no upstream fix was established during this review.
advisories.remaining_fix_scope: A native null-Future validation fix requires a matched Torch/libtorch rebuild and separate CUDA/extension qualification; no rebuild is included.

limitations: Absence of a direct call in the reviewed code is not proof that every indirect library path or custom model is unaffected.
Anyone able to execute arbitrary Python in the process can invoke the affected Torch APIs directly.
Reassess when changing GR00T revisions, checkpoint architecture or quantization, exposing new profiler/RPC inputs, or receiving an upstream fix.
CVE-2026-4538 is handled separately by the documented process-scoped weights-only loading mitigation; that control does not fix these two findings.
